judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports are nearly equivalent in technical substance (a, b, d), but Report 2 explicitly articulates a going-forward policy that doc updates must land in the same commit as the code changes they describe, which Report 1 omits — giving Report 2 a slight edge on expectation (c).

report_1.evidence: New provider calls belong in `medibill/backend/app/billing/gateway.py`... with `app/billing/errors.py` as the only sanctioned exception (it imports just the SDK's exception types, `errors.py:6-9`, and stays within that exception)... `medibill/backend/app/api/invoices.py`... `medibill/backend/app/workers/dunning.py`... That is the complete list.

report_2.evidence: New refund calls should live in `medibill/backend/app/billing/gateway.py`... with `app/billing/errors.py` (which only re-exports the SDK's exception types, `errors.py:6-9`) as the sole exception... `backend/app/api/invoices.py`... `backend/app/workers/dunning.py`... That is the complete list.

report_1.evidence: claims the response contains "exactly" `id, tenant_id, amount_cents, currency, status`. Since commit `c23da88` (MEDB-214, 2026-06-18), the response model `InvoiceOut` also carries `external_ref` (`backend/app/models/invoice.py:22`, serialized at lines 26-28, populated in `invoices.py:17`, backed by `migrations/0006_add_invoice_external_ref.sql`).

report_2.evidence: In the code, `InvoiceOut` has **six** fields — those five plus `external_ref: str | None` (`backend/app/models/invoice.py:16-22`) — and `from_model` serializes `external_ref` into every response (`invoice.py:26-28`)... The field was added in commit `c23da88` (MEDB-214), together with migration `0006_add_invoice_external_ref.sql`.

It should be corrected to match reality **before any refund code is written** — as the first commit of the refund work (or an immediately-preceding standalone commit), not "eventually."... Going forward, treat drift as a merge-blocking bug: any commit that changes the invoice response shape, the webhook set, or the provider boundary must update this doc in the same commit.

report_1.evidence: it is wrong on both the count and the enumeration: the code handles **five** types, the four listed plus `payment_pending`... What I would change about how it is stated: drop the hard-coded count. "Handles 4 webhook event types" is the most fragile possible phrasing... and it failed in exactly the expected way. Restate it to name the source of truth and describe behavior

report_2.evidence: is wrong on both the count and the enumeration. The handler `payment_webhook`... matches five event types... I would change **how it is stated**: drop the hardcoded count entirely. A literal "handles 4" is guaranteed to go stale the next time anyone adds an `if` branch — which is exactly what happened in `c23da88`.
